description: Composite three-panel figure combining two EBSD-derived maps with one electron-channeling-contrast micrograph of a hydrogen-affected Fe-26Mn-11Al-1.2C austenitic steel containing κ-carbides. (a) Inverse pole figure (IPF) map with TD, RD//TA and ND reference axes, a 001-101-111 colour triangle inset and a 50 µm scale bar; grains are coloured by crystallographic orientation and a jagged black crack trace cuts across the map. (b) KAM map of the same area, 50 µm scale bar, with a Min-Max colour legend running 0 (blue) to 5 (red); the crack trace is black and green-to-red strain-localization bands decorate its flanks. A red dashed rectangle labelled "Fig. 17(c)" with the text "Strain localization" locates the region enlarged in (c). (c) Orientation-optimized ECC image, 5 µm scale bar, two dashed lines labelled "Grain boundary", arrows labelled "Strain localization", and several open/black arrows pointing at micro-voids along the boundary. Printed SEM settings: Mag = 5.10 kX, WD = 7.0 mm, EHT = 15.00 kV, Signal A = QBSD, Date: 26 Feb 2013. The panels together demonstrate an intergranular crack following a grain boundary, decorated by localized strain and micro-voids.
measured_quantities: kernel average misorientation (KAM) value, colour bar 0-5 (unit not printed)
scale bar length (µm): 50 µm in (a), 50 µm in (b), 5 µm in (c)

observations.observation: Panel (a) is an IPF orientation map carrying TD and RD//TA reference arrows, an ND marker, a 001-101-111 colour triangle and a 50 µm scale bar.
A jagged, irregular black crack trace runs across the coloured grains of the IPF map in (a), separating differently oriented regions.
Panel (b) is a KAM map with a Min-Max colour legend whose printed values run 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 from blue to red; no unit is printed on the legend.
In (b) the highest KAM values (green through yellow, orange and red) are concentrated in bands flanking the black crack trace, which is itself shown as black.
A red dashed rectangle in (b), labelled 'Fig. 17(c)' and accompanied by the text 'Strain localization', defines the area shown at higher magnification in (c).
Panel (c) is an ECC micrograph with a 5 µm scale bar in which two dashed lines are labelled 'Grain boundary' and arrows labelled 'Strain localization' point along the boundary regions.
In (c) several light-outlined and solid arrows point to small void-like features (micro-voids) arranged along the grain boundary.
Panel (c) prints acquisition metadata: Mag = 5.10 kX, WD = 7.0 mm, EHT = 15.00 kV, Signal A = QBSD, Date: 26 Feb 2013.
The caption identifies the figure as a hydrogen-induced intergranular crack in Fe-26Mn-11Al-1.2C austenitic steel containing κ-carbides (printed as 'Fee26Mne11Ale1.2C').
The caption states that (a) is an inverse pole figure, (b) is a KAM figure, and (c) is an orientation-optimized ECC image corresponding to the part surrounded by the red broken lines in (b).

The citing text states that Koyama et al. [113] proposed that grain-boundary triple-junction cracking and slip-localization-induced intergranular cracking along micro-voids determine the embrittlement ability of the Fe-26Mn-11Al-1.2C steel.
The citing text states that the slip-localization-induced intergranular cracking assisted crack growth during plastic deformation, giving a macroscopically brittle fracture appearance.
The citing text reports that in the earlier Fe-18Mn-1.2C study [112] transgranular fracture initiated parallel to primary and secondary deformation twin boundaries.
